# IEC 60601-1-2 — Medical electrical equipment — Part 1-2: EMC — Electromagnetic disturbances — Requirements and tests

_Demo sample data — not for clinical use._

> **Reference layer**: registry distillation of what the standard says lives at [`.claude/skills/medtech-docs/references/standards/iec-60601-1-2.md`](../../../.claude/skills/medtech-docs/references/standards/iec-60601-1-2.md) (L1a). This file is the **project applicability** layer (L1b) — what the PP3500 program has decided about the standard. Cite both.

**Standard**: IEC 60601-1-2 Edition 4.1 2020-09 CONSOLIDATED VERSION (IEC 60601-1-2:2014 + AMD1:2020) — per the FDA recognition entry; see Edition Determination below for how this maps to the program's "4th edition" citation
**Category**: Medical electrical equipment — EMC (collateral standard to IEC 60601-1)
**Recognized by FDA**: Yes — Recognition Number 19-36, entered 12/21/2020, **partial** recognition; identical US adoption ANSI AAMI IEC 60601-1-2:2014 [Incl. AMD 1:2021]; in the ASCA program. Source: [FDA Recognized Consensus Standards database, record 41539](https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/scripts/cdrh/cfdocs/cfStandards/detail.cfm?standard__identification_no=41539)
**Original Source**: [webstore.iec.ch/en/publication/67554](https://webstore.iec.ch/en/publication/67554)
**Module Applicability**: PP3500 device electronics as a whole — power supply, motor drive, control/pump firmware host electronics, touchscreen UI, and wireless/EHR connectivity hardware. EMC is a whole-equipment property; it is not apportioned per-module the way software standards are.

## Overview

IEC 60601-1-2 governs the PP3500's behavior **in the presence of electromagnetic disturbances** (immunity) and the **disturbances the pump itself emits** (emissions). The 4th edition keys immunity test levels to the intended-use environment (professional healthcare facility / home healthcare / special environments) and judges immunity tests against maintenance of **basic safety and essential performance**, tied to the ISO 14971 risk file. See the L1a reference file (linked above) for the distilled framing and the FDA recognition carve-outs.

## PP3500 Applicability

### Design input — DI-012

[DI-012](../../project/dhfs/pca-device/design-controls/requirements/design-inputs.md) (G4 — Safety & Compliance, category INTE, criticality **CTS**) requires the device to meet the **EMC immunity and emissions requirements of IEC 60601-1-2 (4th edition) for professional healthcare facility environments**. Acceptance criteria: third-party EMC test report; **all immunity tests pass with essential performance maintained**; **emissions within Class B limits**. Traces to UN-018; verification method: EMC test.

Program decisions this encodes:

- **Environment category**: professional healthcare facility — consistent with the PP3500's intended use (hospital PCA therapy under professional supervision) and with the predicate framing. The environment claim in the EMC test report, the IFU, and the risk file must agree.
- **Emissions claim**: Class B limits — the stricter (domestic-capable) emission class [VERIFY against CISPR 11: classification framework per the L1a distillation], a conservative claim for a professional-environment device.
- **Immunity pass/fail**: anchored on **essential performance maintained during immunity exposure** — the 4th edition's core concept. The essential-performance definition (delivery accuracy, alarm function [VERIFY: the program's formal essential-performance list per the IEC 60601-1 record]) supplies the bench pass/fail criteria.

### Hazard analysis — HAZ-010

[HAZ-010](../../project/dhfs/pca-device/risk-management/GL-TMP-RM-003-hazard-analysis.md) — *EMC disturbance disrupting delivery (Energy — electromagnetic)*: RF source near the pump (electrosurgery, RFID, telemetry) couples into pump electronics → delivery error or unintended stop → over- or under-delivery. Pre-control S4/P3 (ALARP); risk control is **EMC immunity and emissions design per IEC 60601-1-2 (4th edition) for professional healthcare facility environments, with essential performance maintained during immunity exposure (DI-012, design)**; post-control S4/P1 (Acceptable).

### Verification evidence

Both DI-012 and HAZ-010 verify through the same artifact: a **third-party EMC test report** — all immunity tests passing with essential performance maintained, emissions within Class B limits. Not yet on file in the DHF [VERIFY: location once design verification produces it].

## Edition Determination — 4th edition vs 4.1

DI-012 and HAZ-010 both cite "**IEC 60601-1-2 (4th edition)**." The FDA database (queried against its 05/2026 revision) lists **Edition 4.1 2020-09 CONSOLIDATED VERSION (Rec# 19-36)** as the only currently recognized version of Part 1-2 — the 2014 base 4th edition no longer appears as a separate active recognition.

- Colloquially, "4th edition" often covers both 4.0 (2014) and the 4.1 consolidation (2014+A1:2020); the program's design-input wording does not distinguish them.
- **[VERIFY — program decision needed]**: pin whether the EMC test campaign and the 510(k) declaration of conformity cite **Edition 4.1 (2020-09 consolidated)**. A DoC citing bare "4th edition 2014" would not match the currently recognized designation. The predicate PP3500 clearance (K210345) EMC citation should also be checked for which designation it carried.
- The FDA recognition is **partial** — two carve-outs (Figure 3 "nursing homes" example; subclause 8.9 Table 8 Note k on SIP/SOP cables < 1 m). The test plan must not rely on either carved-out provision; see the L1a file for details.

## PCCP Considerations

The PP3500 PCCP is software-centric; EMC posture is hardware-and-layout-bound. Any PCCP-governed software change that alters emissions-relevant behavior (e.g., radio duty cycle, clock/power management) or the essential-performance definition used as immunity pass/fail criteria must be evaluated for EMC re-test impact — [VERIFY: against the program's PCCP change-category definitions and FDA's EMC guidance (July 6, 2022) expectations for changes].
